aliases: Discovery of scaling in deep inelastic scattering

claim.quote: Observed Behavior of Highly Inelastic Electron-Proton Scattering

date.note: The data were first reported at the 14th International Conference on High Energy Physics, Vienna, August 1968; Kendall: "By the spring of 1968, the first inelastic results were at hand."
date.quote: 14th Int. Conf. High Energy Phys., Vienna, Aug., 1968. E. D. Bloom et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 23, 930 (1969); M. Breidenbach et al., ibid 23, 935 (1969).

key_value_text.quote: If the interaction is dominated by transverse virtual photons, νW2 can be expressed as a function of ω=2Mνq2 within experimental errors for q2>1 (GeV/c)2 and ω>4
key_value_text.value: νW₂ depends only on ω = 2Mν/q² within experimental errors for q2 > 1 (GeV/c)2 and omega > 4 (scaling)

name: Observed Behavior of Highly Inelastic Electron-Proton Scattering
notes: The paper title says "Observed Behavior", so the type is observation; the quark-model interpretation is in the Nobel press release, not the Letter's abstract.
date is the August 1968 Vienna presentation (month precision); the Letter appeared on 20 October 1969 and its companion (Bloom et al., PRL 23, 930) in the same issue.

published.note: Publication date of the Breidenbach et al. Letter.

summary.plain: Friedman, Kendall, Taylor and colleagues found that electrons scattering hard off protons behaved as if the proton were made of tiny hard pieces. The way the scattering depended on energy and momentum transfer, called scaling, was the first clear sign of quarks.
summary.technical: Inelastic e-p scattering at 6 and 10 degrees: the structure function νW₂ can be expressed as a function of ω = 2Mν/q² alone within experimental errors for q² > 1 (GeV/c)² and ω > 4.

title: Observed Behavior of Highly Inelastic Electron-Proton Scattering
why_it_matters: The 1990 Nobel Prize in Physics went to Friedman, Kendall and Taylor "for their pioneering investigations concerning deep inelastic scattering of electrons on protons and bound neutrons, which have been of essential importance for the development of the quark model in particle physics".
